items.reason: Artifact ordering places exploration after spec and before progress.
Dashboard artifacts consume the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan-markdown exemption includes exploration.md.
Other validation remains intact, including rejection of unlisted markdown.
ExploreRequested reads the set-level explore boolean.
Automatic exploration requires an explicit true value.
ExplorerOverride uses the shared agents-and-effort directive shape.
The guide names both keys and explicitly distinguishes opt-in from opt-out.
The guide states the shared-seam and dependent-later-task rule.
Shared constants feed the guide and manifest readers, with anti-drift tests.
The new command invokes a fresh Explorer with task listings, bodies, and optional spec.
The prompt requests all five required aspects of the existing code.
The prompt requires path-or-symbol evidence, roughly one page, and observed-tree framing.
The prompt excludes a prior-art catalogue and requests no prior-art section.
Successful passes overwrite one flat exploration.md file.
Captured runs and spent retry caps use a distinct explore phase.
Manual exploration bypasses both participation and automatic-exploration gates.
Failed, timed-out, and interrupted agent passes return before report writing.
Integration tests start at exploreResolvedSet; none exercises the command through report and captured-run creation.
Implement prompts conditionally describe the report and provide its path.
The implement template receives only the report pointer, never its body.
The prompt limits edits to lines falsified by the current attempt.
The edit boundary explicitly permits the report beside the task file.
The existing prior-art block is unchanged.
Assist prompts place the exploration pointer beside refinement and recent progress.
Implement and assist goldens cover report-present and report-absent cases.
The drain invokes exploration before entering task selection.
An existing report bypasses exploration without invoking an agent.
Undeclared sets bypass the exploration phase.
The independent work.explore.enabled gate defaults on, including absent configuration.
Disabling automatic exploration prevents its invocation while preserving manual exploration.
Agent and manifest/CLI precedence exists, but no configured exploration effort is supported; effort falls directly to heavy.
HumanCompleted explicitly bypasses automatic exploration.
Report reuse depends on availability, without comparing its recorded SHA to the checkout.
Whole-drain tests cover absent and existing reports and assert Explorer invocation behavior.
The shared fallback walk applies the standard retry cap and delays.
A capped failure followed by a quota-paused fallback leaves the latest run non-parking, allowing implementation without a report.
Park derivation uses captured-run metadata and report absence without schema changes.
EXPLORE-FAILED is distinct from BLOCKED and preserves its human-decision meaning.
Automatic selection and daemon scheduling exclude the parked status.
Manual failures can create a park without progress, while repeated disabled drains append duplicate park records.
The skip flag bypasses exploration and parking for the targeted drain.
Writing a report or withdrawing the declaration removes the derived park.
CONTEXT.md lists EXPLORE-FAILED among drain stops and automatic-selection exclusions.
ExploreMarkBadgeText deliberately suppresses the exploration mark beside EXPLORE-FAILED.
Undeclared sets receive no exploration mark, including after manual exploration.
Refresh resolves exploration centrally and passes that result to all four surfaces.
Dashboard detail renders the report path and recorded tree without its body.
The sign-off preamble includes exploration alongside the refine-report pointer.

scores.rationale: Broad implementation and substantial tests, but failure aggregation, park logging, configured effort, and command-level coverage leave meaningful gaps.

accepted.behaviour: Tests drive the whole explore path together: the command, the agent reply, the report on disk and the captured run row, not each piece separately.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 02 criteria) says that tests drive the whole path, starting at the command. The Reference tests start at `exploreResolvedSet` and never run `pop tasks explore`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: The manifest's `explorer` object overrides the configured agent list and effort for the explore pass, and CLI flags override the `explorer` object.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 04 criteria) says that the `explorer` object overrides the configured agent list and the configured effort. The Reference has no configured Explorer effort: `resolveExplorer` falls back to `DefaultExploreEffort`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: A declared set whose explore pass gave up and wrote no report shows a park status of its own (for example EXPLORE-FAILED), and the drain stops at that status.
accepted.reason: The spec says a set whose explore pass gave up parks instead of building blind. The Reference misses one path: a capped failure followed by a quota-paused fallback leaves the latest run non-parking.

accepted.behaviour: When a set parks, exactly one set-level progress record is added. It names the explore phase and the reason.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 05 criteria) says that the park appends exactly one set-level progress record. In the Reference, only the drain's `parkUnexplored` writes the record. A failed hand-run pass parks the set with no record, and repeated drains append one record each time. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.

accepted.behaviour: A set that declared `explore` and has no report shows an exploration mark beside its status. The reason (not yet run, or the pass failed) appears as detail beside the mark, not inside the mark's value.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 06 criteria) says that a declared set with no report carries the mark beside its status, with the reason "the pass failed" as detail. In the Reference, `ExploreMarkBadgeText` returns an empty mark for a parked set. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.
